articles.title: Singapore and the UAE to launch economic partnership negotiations to further trade, investment links
articles.summary: Singapore and the UAE began economic partnership talks in Abu Dhabi. Leaders signed three agreements covering energy, water, and disease control. articles.summary: Families report ICE is deporting severely ill detainees from Florida jails. Flights to unknown African countries are scheduled for Wednesday. articles.title: Peace efforts resume to end ‘drone war’ fuelling humanitarian crisis
articles.summary: Sudan peace talks resumed in Geneva on Wednesday. Nearly two dozen countries met to discuss a ceasefire. The goal is a transition to peaceful governance that represents all Sudanese people amid the ongoing drone war. articles.title: Global warming will breach 1.5°C – but deep, fast cuts can still bring it back
articles.summary: Global temperatures will exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Nations must implement deep, rapid emissions cuts to minimize this overshoot. articles.title: US Citizen Accused By Moscow Of Fighting For Ukraine Released From Russian Prison
articles.summary: Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired Michigan teacher, was released from Russian custody. He had been detained since 2022 on charges of joining Ukraine's armed forces. articles.title: Wounded Ukrainian Soldier Rescued From Front Lines By Aerial Drone
articles.summary: Ukraine's military rescued a wounded soldier from the front lines using an aerial drone. The soldier, injured in both legs, strapped himself to a hexacopter for evacuation. Fellow servicemen described the act as heroic. This marks the first recorded instance of such a drone-based battlefield rescue. In what Ukraine's military is calling a historic first, a soldier who suffered injuries to both legs on the battlefield was evacuated by an unmanned aerial drone.

articles.summary: Georgia’s Constitutional Court will begin hearings on October 21 regarding a ban on five opposition parties. These parties have collectively won hundreds of thousands of votes. articles.summary: Over 250,000 people have fled renewed fighting in Yemen, the United Nations reported. Access to the southwestern city of Taiz is essentially blocked. This has trapped residents in areas facing severe hunger and disease. The displacement continues to strain local humanitarian resources. articles.summary: Moldova launched an investigation into Yandex for allegedly harvesting citizen data. The company reportedly sent personal information to Russian servers instead of the Netherlands. This contradicts previous data storage agreements. The probe follows an investigation by Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty. Moldova has announced an investigation into concerns that Russian tech giant Yandex has been harvesting the personal data of its citizens by sending it directly to servers in Russia rather than storing it in the Netherlands as previously believed.

articles.title: Why Starshield’s slowdown really hurts Ukraine
articles.summary: SpaceX temporarily restricted Starshield satellite internet for Ukrainian forces. This slowdown has raised serious concerns in Kyiv and among its allies. articles.summary: Zelenskyy thanked the United States after Oslo talks. He said missile intelligence now works effectively. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner joined the meetings. articles.summary: Saudi Arabia executed two Bangladeshis on October 14, prompting minimal diplomatic reaction from Dhaka. articles.summary: A Russian military satellite passed exceptionally close to a Finnish-operated satellite. The Finnish satellite provides intelligence to Ukraine. articles.title: Funding cuts leave half a million without food assistance
articles.summary: The World Food Programme cut Gaza aid by one third due to funding shortages. The reduction leaves roughly 500,000 people without food assistance as winter approaches, the UN agency announced on Monday. Funding shortages have forced the World Food Programme (WFP) to slash assistance to hungry families in the Gaza Strip by roughly one third – a move that will affect some 500,000 people as winter approaches, the UN agency announced on Monday.

articles.title: Guterres honours Indonesian troops who paid ‘ultimate sacrifice’
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres honored four Indonesian peacekeepers killed in Lebanon. UN Secretary-General António Guterres paid tribute to Indonesian peacekeepers on Monday, laying a wreath in honour of four who recently lost their lives in Lebanon and offering a robust defence of UN peacekeeping in what he called “testing times for peace”.

articles.title: Protecting Earth’s fragile biodiversity takes spotlight at Armenia talks
articles.summary: The UN Biodiversity Conference opened in Yerevan, Armenia. The top UN official warned that ongoing biodiversity losses threaten the prosperity of billions. He urged nations to take immediate action to protect the planet. Biodiversity losses continue to upend the lives of billions of people whose future prosperity depends on countries taking urgent action to protect our planet, the top UN official leading talks at the UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, said on Monday.

articles.title: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods
articles.summary: Hurricane Trudy weakened to a tropical storm after threatening Mexico's Pacific coast. The system remained 160 kilometers southwest of the shore. articles.title: ऐसे प्रदर्शन तो रोज होते हैं... CJP प्रोटेस्ट पर पूछा गया सवाल, मार्को रुबियो के जवाब ने चौंकाया?
articles.summary: अमेरिकी विदेश मंत्री मार्को रुबियो ने भारत में सीजेपी प्रदर्शनों पर टिप्पणी करते हुए कहा कि अमेरिका में ऐसे प्रदर्शन रोज होते हैं। उन्होंने भारत सरकार की आलोचना को खारिज कर दिया। यहां आने से पहले ही उनसे पूछा गया कि वे भारत में चल रहे प्रदर्शनों पर क्या कहना चाहेंगे, जब यूएन ने इसे लेकर टिप्पणी की है. किसी ने नहीं सोचा था कि मार्को रुबियो ऐसा जवाब देंगे, जैसा उन्होंने दिया.
